title: Parties backend: list, detail with leads card, create/update with duplicate warning
objective: Port the Parties API: tenant-scoped list with filters/search/sort/paging, detail including the party-leads data, and create/update with non-blocking duplicate-name warning and format-validated contact fields; no deletion (P-05).
scope: GET /api/v1/parties (filters, search, sort, paging), POST, GET /{id}, PUT /{id}, GET /{id}/leads per reference contract
Name required; non-blocking duplicate warning in the warnings payload; optional region; contact fields format-validated; party type from reference list
Tenant isolation + breadth-agnostic visibility per reference behavior
out_of_scope: Lead creation (T-024 — party picker consumes this API)
implementation_details: Mirror .NET Parties endpoints; pagination envelope {items,page,pageSize,total} default 25; sort/filter params preserved.
Duplicate check: same normalized name within tenant produces warnings:[...] but allows proceed (verify normalization rules from the .NET validator and port them).
GET /{id}/leads returns the leads-card data used by the party detail page (columns per reference DTO).

integration: List pagination/search/sort/filters against fixtures; create/update validation catalog (name required, contact formats); duplicate warning present but non-blocking
Party leads card data correct; tenant isolation (404 cross-tenant); no DELETE route exists

findings.description: M5's 'unfalsifiable by black-box test' claim is WRONG, so the leads-card brokers-join tenant predicate is an unguarded defense-in-depth line: dropping `b.tenant_id = ${tenantId}` from listLeadsForParty (parties/repository.ts:551-552) leaves the ENTIRE suite green (evaluator reproduced: mutant proven applied by grep 0/1 + md5 delta, parties.test.ts 67/67 passed exit 0), yet the predicate has an observable, constructible behavioural difference. The implementor's globally-unique-id reasoning holds only for CONVENTION-RESPECTING data; the schema itself permits the discriminating state because leads.broker_id carries NO physical FK (brokers migration :47: 'by convention, no FK'). A lead whose broker_id points at another tenant's broker is insertable with plain SQL - exactly what this repo's integration fixtures do routinely - and under the mutant GET /parties/{id}/leads then LEAKS the other tenant's broker NAME, while pristine code correctly answers brokerName null. With RLS not adopted (Q-10) there is nothing beneath this predicate, and the honest 'NO coverage' admission means a future refactor can drop it with every gate green.
findings.evidence: Evaluator probe on the live schema (single transaction, rolled back): created a broker in tenant T2, then a party and a lead in tenant T1 with broker_id = the T2 broker's id - ALL inserts succeeded, no constraint fired. The leads-card join WITH the predicate returned broker_name NULL; WITHOUT the predicate it returned 'M5-PROBE-FOREIGN-BROKER', the tenant-T2 name. That is a red/green discriminator reachable from an integration test through the real endpoint. Mutant restored byte-identical (md5 c1b759c9) and parties.test.ts re-verified green.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one integration test to parties.test.ts: seed (direct SQL, as fixtures already do) a tenant-A lead whose broker_id equals a tenant-B broker's id, call GET /parties/{id}/leads as tenant A, and assert the row appears with brokerName null (and that no tenant-B name string occurs anywhere in the response). Re-run the M5 mutant afterwards and confirm it goes red. Consider whether the sibling per-join predicates in the same SQL (reference_items x3, lead_assignments, business_assignments) warrant the same corrupt-reference treatment - the brokers join is the one that leaks a NAME, so it is the priority; the inner joins on reference_items make the lead VANISH from its own tenant's card instead, which is lower stakes but same class. KEEP the predicate itself - this finding is about guarding it, not doubting it.
findings.evaluator_confirmation: Iteration-1 evaluator independently re-verified every claim in this resolution first-hand (2026-07-19): M5 mutant re-run killed by exactly the new test with the discriminating assertion (brokerName leak message named the actual foreign name, not a status change); application proven (predicate count 1->0, md5 c1b759c9->6b7ef9d9); restored md5-identical and suite re-verified 68/68. Live-DB similarity measured: old-style token unrelated pair 0.418 (false positive reproduced), new-token unrelated 0.275, new-token Acme pair 0.750, names-alone 0.000/0.615 — margin in both directions confirmed, and detection provably rides on the names (Acme pair clears the threshold with no token at all), so the fix did not suppress detection. ONE INACCURACY: the residue this resolution attributes to 'evaluator mutant runs' is actually left by EVERY run of this suite, including pristine passing ones — see F-023-2.
findings.resolution: Added the corrupt-reference test the finding prescribed: a tenant-A lead whose broker_id is a tenant-B broker id (seeded by direct SQL, which the schema permits because leads.broker_id has NO physical FK), then GET /parties/{id}/leads as tenant A asserting brokerName is null, that the lead itself is STILL listed (the join is LEFT, so a corrupt reference must not make the tenant's own lead vanish), and that the foreign broker name appears NOWHERE in the raw response body. M5 RE-RUN AND NOW KILLED: dropping `b.tenant_id = ${tenantId}` from the brokers LEFT JOIN fails exactly this one test (1 failed / 67 passed); application proven by predicate count 1->0 plus an md5 delta, restored md5-identical. The evaluator was right and the implementor's globally-unique-id argument was too narrow: it covered convention-respecting data only, while the predicate exists precisely for convention-violating data the schema allows. A SECOND, PRE-EXISTING DEFECT WAS EXPOSED WHILE FIXING THIS and is also fixed here. Adding one party fixture turned the "emits no warning at all for a name with no near-duplicate" test RED. Root cause measured, not guessed: duplicate detection is trigram similarity over the WHOLE name, and the run token (`t023-<pid>-<ms>`, ~23 chars) was longer than the names under test, so every fixture in a run shared a dominant block of trigrams. Two utterly unrelated names scored 0.410 against each other - just over the 0.4 threshold - purely on the shared suffix, versus 0.000 on the names alone. The negative-warning tests were therefore riding the threshold and would have broken for the NEXT task that added any party fixture, exactly like the tenants.test.ts entity_id class. Fixed by shortening RUN to a short base36 token (the `t023-` prefix is load-bearing for the stale-fixture purge and was kept): unrelated names now score 0.22-0.25 while the genuine "Acme Insurance Ltd" vs "Acme Insurance Limited" pair scores 0.73 - a real margin in BOTH directions, verified against the live DB. The positive duplicate tests still pass, so the fix did not simply suppress detection. Gates: 66 files / 1279 passed / 0 skipped exit 0, typecheck 0 after the full run, lint 0, ci:test floor 1279. Stale fixture residue purged (27 parties, 10 t020ba tenants left by evaluator mutant runs). Orchestrator-verified only; queued for the next evaluator round.

findings.description: parties.test.ts's afterAll tenant-fixture cleanup is a silent no-op on EVERY exit, normal or aborted: afterAll calls auth.cleanup() (line 550) BEFORE the deleteTenantData loop (552-554), auth.cleanup() ends the pg pool (tests/helpers/auth.ts:249), so every subsequent delete throws on the ended pool and is swallowed by deleteTenantData's .catch(() => undefined). The suite's own comment ('afterAll cleans up on a normal exit', line 182) is false, and the F-023-1 resolution's attribution of residue to 'evaluator mutant runs' is wrong — every run leaks. The beforeAll purge (built for aborted runs) is what actually carries cleanup, one run late: residue (28 parties, 10 leads, 19 audit_log rows, 2 tenants per run) sits in the shared DB until the NEXT parties run, and tenants.test.ts's unfiltered audit_log entity_id count — the exact fragility this task itself documented and OBSERVED failing — can collide with the leftover party audit rows if it executes before parties' beforeAll in a subsequent run. NON-BLOCKING and partly CROSS-TASK: the same broken ordering exists in brokers.test.ts:388-393, business-assignments.test.ts:401-404, business-rules.test.ts:313-316, reference-data.test.ts:367-374, and worse leaks exist in suites with NO purge at all (live DB right now holds 7 t016 tenants, 6 pairs of t019 tenants, plus t020ba/t020br residue after a fully green run); me.test.ts:293-297 and roles-groups.test.ts:330-333 show the CORRECT ordering already in-repo.
findings.evidence: Empirical, live DB: ran the full suite (66 files / 1279 passed, exit 0) — tenants 524/525 (t023-182gzwpt-*) and all child rows survived; ran parties.test.ts alone green (68/68) — it purged 524/525 in beforeAll and left its OWN pair (565/566) plus 28 parties / 10 leads / 2 brokers / 19 audit_log / 4 user_tenants / 16 reference_items rows behind. Each run cleans the previous run's mess, never its own, which is why the leak was invisible.
findings.suggested_fix: In parties.test.ts's afterAll, move the deleteTenantData loop ABOVE auth?.cleanup() (the ordering me.test.ts and roles-groups.test.ts already use). Recommend the orchestrator route the sibling suites (brokers, business-assignments, business-rules, reference-data, and the purge-less t016/t019 suites) as one cross-task hygiene sweep rather than bouncing each task individually.

F-023-1 resolved by the orchestrator, plus a second latent defect it exposed. The finding itself was a genuinely excellent catch: the evaluator refuted an "unfalsifiable by black-box test" claim EMPIRICALLY, by constructing the state the schema permits rather than arguing about it - a missing physical FK meant a cross-tenant broker reference was insertable, and the unguarded join leaked the foreign broker name. Evaluator PASS at iteration 1/10 after a focused re-review of the two fixes from the F-023-1 round, BOTH INDEPENDENTLY CONFIRMED FIRST-HAND. (1) F-023-1 fix VERIFIED BY RE-RUNNING M5 MYSELF: baseline parties.test.ts 68/68 green; mutant applied with proof (grep 'on b.tenant_id' 1->0, md5 c1b759c9->6b7ef9d9 - the file is UNTRACKED so git diff is blind and hash discipline was mandatory); under the mutant EXACTLY the new corrupt-reference test failed (1 failed / 67 passed) and on the DISCRIMINATING assertion - AssertionError 'resolved a broker across the tenant boundary: expected Foreign Broker B t023-... to be null' at parties.test.ts:1341, i.e. the actual foreign broker NAME leaking, not a status change; restored byte-identical (md5 back to c1b759c9, predicate count 1) and re-verified 68/68. Test is non-hollow: the LEFT-join still-listed assertion, the brokerName-null assertion, and the raw-body not.toContain are all present, and the not.toContain is guarded against a hollow pass by toBeTruthy() on the fetched foreign name (:1313). (2) RUN-token defect VERIFIED AGAINST THE LIVE DB, not by reading code: old-style ~23-char token makes two unrelated fixture names score 0.418 (> the 0.4 threshold - the false positive reproduced); the new short token scores the same unrelated pair 0.275 and the genuine Acme Ltd/Limited pair 0.750 - real margin in BOTH directions; names alone score 0.000 vs 0.615, so the positive duplicate tests clear the threshold on the NAMES THEMSELVES with no token at all - the fix demonstrably did NOT suppress detection, and the positive tests (:830 warning code + specific match id/name + row physically present; :895 update path) remain load-bearing. The t023- purge prefix confirmed kept and load-bearing (:127, :192). deviations_and_flags: TASK-FILE CONTRADICTION (list envelope): implementation_details say {items,page,pageSize,total}. Reference PartyListDto.cs:67 and the existing SPA (src/ui/src/features/parties/partiesApi.ts) both say totalCount. Shipped totalCount (measured contract wins) and pinned it with a test; shipping total would break the existing grid's paging.

TASK-FILE CONTRADICTION (duplicate detection): implementation_details describe 'same normalized name within tenant', i.e. normalize-then-compare-equal. The reference does NOT normalize; PartyStore.cs:189-206 runs pg_trgm similarity(name,$1) >= 0.4. Ported the actual trigram behaviour. Consequently the test-plan item 'duplicate-name normalization rules (pure)' has only a small genuinely-pure surface (the persisted-name trim plus the threshold constants), which is what party-name-matching.test.ts covers; the similarity behaviour is proven in the integration suite against real rows rather than against a reimplemented scorer.

MEASURED, EASY TO GET WRONG: GET /parties/{id}/leads is gated by parties.view, not leads.view (LeadEndpoints.cs:40, despite the route living in LeadEndpoints). Pinned with a user holding parties.view and NOT leads.view, and a user holding leads.view and NOT parties.view.

Leads card flags is ALWAYS an empty array - the reference does the same (LeadDto.cs:149-153); the Escalated/SLA/Expiring/High-value chips come from alert evaluation, which is out of T-023's scope. Empty is the correct answer here, not a stub.
Leads card premium is always estimated_premium; the 'current quoted premium once quoted' branch is a later task's seam, exactly as in the reference (LeadDto.cs:134-138).

DIVERGENCE IN SHAPE (not behaviour): the reference issued 4 queries for the leads card (leads join, then owners, then broker names); this port issues 1 with LEFT JOINs, to avoid the N+1-adjacent pattern CLAUDE.md forbids. Added an 'id desc' tiebreaker to the reference's bare 'date_received desc', which was non-deterministic among same-day leads.

List query params: an unparseable filter value is IGNORED, not rejected (ASP.NET binds null for a long?/bool? that will not parse), so ?partyTypeId=abc lists everything rather than 400ing. Ported deliberately and pinned; rejecting would turn a currently-200 hand-edited URL into an error.

Contact email/phone: the reference's .When(!string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(...)) guard means an ALL-WHITESPACE value is VALID. Ported as a refinement rather than zod's .email(), which would have rejected it and turned a currently-200 SPA request into a 422. Pinned by test.

Missing/malformed X-Tenant-Id answers 403, not 400 - the documented house contract (lib/tenancy/middleware.ts:11-31, TenantContextMiddleware.cs:50-55), so a client cannot distinguish 'no header' from 'not your tenant'. My initial test asserted 400 and was corrected to match the real, deliberate contract.

CROSS-TASK FINDING (flagged, not fixed here): tenants.test.ts asserts count(*) from audit_log where entity_id = $1 WITHOUT filtering entity_type. Any other suite's leftover audit row whose entity_id numerically equals the tenant id under test makes tenants.test.ts fail with no clue why. This suite triggered it after an ABORTED run left party audit rows behind. Guarded from this side (parties.test.ts now purges stale t023- tenants in beforeAll, so an interrupted run cannot poison later runs) and tenants.test.ts verified green again - but the underlying assertion remains fragile for any future suite.
